reference.title: Programmatic bootstrap configuration fields
reference.shortdesc: Use these configuration fields to control bootstrap OAuth token provisioning for automated Red Hat Quay deployments. The feature remains disabled until you enable it. Standalone deployments store the token in a local file. Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform Operator deployments store the token in a Kubernetes Secret that the Operator creates and mounts.

entry.p: Enables programmatic bootstrap token provisioning. When true, Red Hat Quay creates a bootstrap OAuth token on startup and writes it to a local file or Kubernetes Secret. When false, Red Hat Quay revokes any existing bootstrap token on restart.
Username that owns the bootstrap OAuth application and token. Required when FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP is true. The user must exist in the database and be listed in SUPER_USERS.

Filesystem path where the bootstrap token JSON is written on standalone and virtual machine deployments. In containerized deployments, use a mounted path that the Red Hat Quay process can write, for example /datastorage/bootstrap-token.json.
Space-separated OAuth scopes assigned to the bootstrap token.

p.codeph: org:admin repo:admin repo:create repo:read repo:write super:user user:admin user:read

entry.p: Kubernetes Secret name used to store the bootstrap token when Red Hat Quay runs in Kubernetes. When set, Red Hat Quay writes the token to this Secret instead of BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_PATH. On Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform, the Operator sets this field to <quayregistry_name>-bootstrap-token when programmatic bootstrap is enabled. Do not set this field manually in Operator-managed deployments.
Secret data key that stores the bootstrap token JSON. On Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform, the Operator sets this field to token.json.

Kubernetes namespace that contains the bootstrap token Secret. When unset, Red Hat Quay uses the pod service account namespace. On Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform, the Operator uses the QuayRegistry namespace.

Operator-rendered mount path for configuration compatibility. On Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform, the Operator sets this field to /var/lib/quay/bootstrap-token/token.json. Standalone deployments use BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_PATH for local file storage.

section.codeblock: FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP: true SUPER_USERS: - quayadmin BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_OWNER: quayadmin BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_PATH: /var/lib/quay/quay-machine-token.json BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_EXPIRATION: 7776000 BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_SCOPE: "org:admin repo:admin repo:create repo:read repo:write super:user user:admin user:read"

p.b: Programmatic bootstrap example YAML (Red Hat Quay on OpenShift Container Platform configBundleSecret)

section.codeblock: FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP: true SUPER_USERS: - quayadmin BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_OWNER: quayadmin BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_EXPIRATION: 7776000 BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_SCOPE: "org:admin repo:admin repo:create repo:read repo:write super:user user:admin user:read"

note.p: For Operator deployments, omit BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_PATH and the PROGRAMMATIC_TOKEN_K8S_* fields from the configBundleSecret. The Operator injects PROGRAMMATIC_TOKEN_K8S_SECRET, PROGRAMMATIC_TOKEN_K8S_KEY, and PROGRAMMATIC_TOKEN_PATH, and creates the <quayregistry_name>-bootstrap-token Secret, Role, and RoleBinding automatically.
Always quote BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_SCOPE. Unquoted values that contain : can be misparsed by YAML.

The bootstrap token is a high-privilege credential. Use it only to provision organizations, applications, and narrower-scoped OAuth tokens for automation. Do not use the bootstrap token for routine API operations.
For regulated environments, set BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_EXPIRATION according to your token rotation policy and renew the token by using POST /api/v1/bootstrap/renew.
